checks.control: JWT authentication on protected API routes
checks.evidence: Protected transaction and data routes use JWT middleware.

checks.control: Role enforcement for authority workflow actions
checks.evidence: Approval, finalization, analytics and ledger verification require authority/admin role.

checks.control: Current claimant required before transfer proposal
checks.evidence: Workflow policy checks the authenticated account against the current claimant reference.
Only workflow-reviewed claims can enter a transfer workflow.

checks.control: Public registration cannot create authority/admin accounts
checks.evidence: Authority roles are excluded from public signup.
A source file digest is persisted for integrity tracking.
Document validation runs before event submission.
File extension/MIME allowlist plus PDF/image signature and text binary checks.
Application ledger hash chain can be verified by authority users.
Nested payload objects are included in deterministic hash serialization.
Claim submissions and buyer workflow transactions require an application-service certificate.
Approval and finalization require a separate authority certificate.
Public channel state stores keyed references instead of raw owner names, parcel identifiers, addresses or account IDs.

checks.control: Strong HMAC key required for Fabric references
checks.evidence: Application requires a 32-byte HMAC secret and chaincode validates HMAC references.

note: Static source-control audit only. It is not dynamic security testing, penetration testing, identity proofing, or certification of deployed Fabric credentials.
